data._missing_nav_note: AS FOR THE CORE (team lead 2026-10-29): gate 5's missing-NAV hold, quantt/session/gate.py missing_nav_hold. A fund whose only fault is a NAV not dated the as-of date DEFERS the decide before the final check (close - 90 min, 14:30 ET) and from the final check is HELD at its current shares, out of the cross-section, while the others decide. AGE LIMIT 2 consecutive sessions, the team lead's POLICY for the core, carried, not derived for C4: after it the day is refused, naming the fund. The name limit is derived by the runner from the C4 spec's min_names (74 - 6 = 68). Why it matters more here: C4's NAVs come from yfinance alone (no CEFConnect, below), so a late NAV is never filled from a second source; fetch_daily --data-book c4 exits 4 and the hold is what keeps one late fund from costing the other 73 the day. STILL REFUSED: a missing or stale close, a fund with no NAV at all, any refresh failure other than exit 4 (including exit 6, the spike guard: an unruled spike-and-revert bar in the fetched window), and more missing NAVs than 68. Exit 6 is refused on a day a NAV is late too: fetch_daily exits 6 OVER its INCOMPLETE exit 4 (release-check of 8b14298, 2026-11-02; until then exit 4 outranked 6, so at the final check this hold accepted the 4 and the session decided on the unruled bar; quantt/session/tests/test_c4_book.py test_at_the_final_check_an_unruled_spike_refuses_c4_even_with_a_late_nav). READ BY quantt/session/run.py missing_nav_for and missing_nav_max_sessions_for. NO data.stale_nav ON PURPOSE: the stale-NAV gate reads CEFConnect, which is disabled for C4 (team lead 2026-10-28, plan section 3 item 3), and locks and logs as the core's fetch_daily; run.stale_nav_panel refuses it for any NAV file but the core's. C4's defence against a stale NAV is the spec's NAV-repeat mask M1 (frozen.nav_repeat_mask), and the collector reports each fund-day M1 removes (quantt/collect BOOKS['c4'] step nav_repeats). REVERT: delete these three keys and the block (gate 5 then refuses the day on one missing NAV).

corporate_actions._note: AS FOR THE CORE: the team lead's 2026-10-28 ruling is a HALT guard 'for the paper runner', and C4 trades on the same paper runner. Alpaca paper processes no splits or mergers, so a held fund that splits keeps its old share count at the new price and the plan is sized on the wrong exposure; C4's own history has one (IGR's 1:3 reverse split, effective 2026-09-08, whose four post-split-basis bars the seed rules on). At every decide, and again at the late-market send, the runner reads Alpaca's non-dividend corporate actions for every held and targeted name and REFUSES the session (a gate-5 data refusal, exit 11) on one inside its window, or when the feed cannot be read (quantt/session/corp_actions.py; windows ruled 2026-10-29). The read is one market-wide query, filtered locally, so 74 names add no requests. A long-window halt on a held name clears only through docs/RUNBOOK.md section 6.1, orders through the team lead. Set here by the integration of 2026-10-29, not by a separate ruling for C4: REVERT to the session without the gate by deleting this block, or set 'report' to record and send anyway.
